Practised the pattern that sums of consecutive odd numbers starting at 1 form square numbers.
Worked through 1+3+5+7=16 and 1+3+5+7+9=25.
Used dot patterns to find that adding to a 5×5 square requires 9 dots.
For 1 through 29, identified 15 odd numbers and calculated 15²=225.
Teach-back was not yet passed; 0 unaided correct attempts across 3 attempts.
end.parentNote: Saanvi practised connecting consecutive odd-number sums with square numbers and used a dot-grid method to explain why the next layer adds an odd number of dots. They corrected the 5×5 to 6×6 addition by accounting for the overlapping corner, changing 10 to 9. At home, ask them to draw a 3×3 or 4×4 dot square and explain how many dots the next layer adds.
